_meta.description: STARTER/REPRESENTATIVE clause set authored for the hackathon MVP demo. Paraphrased from well-known, publicly documented provisions of Indian data-privacy/security regulation for demo purposes. NOT verified against primary legal text — before any real customer-facing use, have this checked against the actual DPDP Act 2023 text, RBI Cyber Security Framework circulars, and CERT-In Directions 2022.
_meta.action_item: Someone (HR/PM) should replace this with verified clause citations sourced from official government publications before the pitch, or clearly caveat in the demo that citations are illustrative.

clauses.summary: A Data Fiduciary should only process personal data for the specific purpose consented to, and should not retain broader access than that purpose requires.
Personal data transferred to or processed by entities outside India may be subject to government-notified restrictions; organizations are expected to know where their data is processed and by whom.
Any third-party service that processes personal data on a company's behalf is a Data Processor, and the company (as Data Fiduciary) remains accountable for that processor's handling of the data.
Personal data breaches must be reported to the Data Protection Board and affected individuals without undue delay.
Regulated entities are expected to periodically review third-party and vendor access, and de-provision access that is no longer in active use.
Certain classes of cybersecurity incidents must be reported to CERT-In within a fixed short window (commonly cited as 6 hours) of being noticed.
Access grants should be scoped to the minimum permission level needed, and should be revoked when a tool becomes dormant or is no longer needed for its original purpose.

SEBI-regulated entities (exchanges, depositories, brokers, mutual funds, KYC agencies) must assess third-party and vendor risk as part of their cybersecurity compliance framework, tiered by entity size.
Critical systems must maintain a Software Bill of Materials — a documented inventory of exactly what software/components are running and where they came from.
Insurers and intermediaries must manage third-party and vendor risk under a board-approved cybersecurity policy, with regular VAPT.
Policyholder data must be stored in compliance with IRDAI's localization requirements; incidents involving this data must be reported to IRDAI within a defined timeline.
